purpose: Ofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections in different parts of the body. It can treat infections of the urinary tract, lungs, skin, and certain sexually transmitted infections. It also comes as ear drops for ear infections and eye drops for eye infections.
how_it_works: Ofloxacin works by attacking the DNA of bacteria, stopping them from being able to copy themselves and grow. Think of it like cutting the bacteria's instruction manual so they cannot reproduce. This allows your immune system to clear the infection more easily.
common_side_effects: You may notice nausea, stomach upset, diarrhea, or headache. Some people feel dizzy or have trouble sleeping. The eye drops may cause mild stinging or itching, and the ear drops may cause temporary ear discomfort. Most side effects are mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Avoid too much sun exposure while taking this medication, as it can make your skin burn more easily. Rarely, this drug can cause tendon problems, especially in your Achilles tendon — stop taking it and call your doctor if you feel sudden tendon pain. Tell your doctor if you have seizures, kidney problems, or heart rhythm issues. This antibiotic is not recommended for children or pregnant women unless absolutely necessary.
typical_dosing: For most infections, adults take 200 to 400 mg by mouth every 12 hours for 7 to 14 days, depending on the type of infection. Eye drops are usually 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye every 2 to 4 hours. Ear drops are typically 5 to 10 drops in the affected ear once or twice daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and finish the full course even if you feel better.
